source_read: https://docs.baynes.co.uk/Allergens-Website.pdf (4 pages, MASTER Allergens.xlsx, version 108, issue 06.10.26, sha256 a12ff4fb9eba528947d89d9f83da9b2fa7e3a8fb2d2d78724871e886bcc9b434) and https://baynes.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nutritional-Website-1.pdf (sha256 b585160030856373cbdab6aa1ad5e919ad67f037e87b0b383b358cddb7fa0517), both downloaded fresh 2026-10-08, one GET each, after reading robots.txt (baynes.co.uk allows everything; docs.baynes.co.uk has no robots.txt, 404). Byte-identical to the files the nutrition script was written against.
notes: Result: 145 published items now carry allergens copied from the guide's grid (allergens.csv, 146 lines); 32 of the 178 nutrition rows (18%, under the one-third limit) are not published because the guide has no exact row for them (31) or the row contradicts the name (1); the 3 existing nutrition holdbacks are unchanged (2 of them are also in the 32). How the grid is read: the 17 allergen columns are coloured cells with no text, so baynes_pdf.read_allergens reads the page's vector fills (pdftocairo -svg): green = contains, two light-grey tints (82.35% and 85.10%, different Excel cell styles; the whole of page 4 uses the lighter one) = not marked; any other fill, a point with no fill, or three samples disagreeing stops the run; the 17 rotated header labels are checked on every page; and each row's 'Suitable for Vegetarians' cell fill (peach for YES, grey for NO) is checked against the printed text, which proves the row height was right (negative tests: swapped headers, rows shifted 12 pt, unknown fill, missing fill, oat-drink rule removed: all stop the run). Independent check, a different method: pdftoppm 150 dpi raster, rows located from the product-name text line (not the vegetarian flag), colours classified from pixel values in the middle of every cell: all 168 rows x 17 cells agree with the vector reading (0 differences), and all 145 published allergens.csv rows (contains, cereals, may contain) agree with the pixels (0 mismatches). Also read by eye: 32 randomly chosen published rows (seed 7) on cropped renders of the source next to the CSV text, plus the header band: 0 differences (checked: macaroni-pie, chocolate-eclair, pink-iced-doughring, cabin-roll, cheese-and-onion-pasty, tuna-mayonnaise-salad-filled-morning-rolls, chicken-and-bacon, mr-blobby-biscuit, cappuccino-large, traditional-morning-loaf, fudge-cream-doughnut, bran-roll, cheese-savoury-salad (morning and rye), simply-ham-filled-rye-rolls, salad-no-filling, cheese-and-ham, ham-and-cheese-baguette-melt, scotch-pie, black-coffee-regular, rye-roll, iced-latte, cappuccino-regular, strawberry-sponge, chicken-mayonnaise-salad, lemon-and-ginger-tea, strawberry-flan, individual-trifle, sweet-and-spicy-chicken-pasty, iced-vanilla-latte, sous-lug, egg-mayonnaise). Mapping: a nutrition row takes the allergen row with the same section heading and the same printed name; no similar-name matching. The four gluten columns name the cereal (oats, rye, barley, wheat); '(Tree) Nuts' names no nut; marks across the 145 published rows: gluten 119, milk 99, eggs 62, soya 61, sulphites 29, fish 7, celery 1, sesame 1; no published row marks crustaceans, lupin, molluscs, mustard, peanut or tree nuts. May contain: the grid has no may-contain column; the PDF's own sentence says its oat alternative hot drinks 'may contain traces of Cow's Milk' and a footnote '*May contain Milk' marks the five '... Oat Milk Drink' coffees (not published: no exact nutrition row), so the only published row covered, 'Tea with Oat Drink', is recorded as may contain milk (the script stops if any other published item names an oat drink or if the sentence/footnote disappear). The general paragraph (nuts, cereals, egg, soya, milk, fish, celery, mustard, sesame and sulphites used in the bakery, separation not guaranteed) is not item data and is in note.txt only; may_contain_published stays 'yes'. Held back, with a reason in holdback.csv: all 12 'Filled Dark Fired Rolls' (the allergen PDF has no such section), 'Shell Steak Pie' (guide: 'Steak Pie'), 'Apple Puff' ('Apple Turnover'), 'Empire Biscuit with jelly sweet' ('...Sweet'), 'White French Cake with Lilac Drizzle' ('French Cake with Lilac Drizzle**'), 'Gingerbread' ('Plain Gingerbread'), 'Omelette (1 piece)' ('Vegetarian Omelette'), 'Hot Chocolate' ('Hot Chocolate (12oz)'), the four 'Tetley/Twining's Tea ... (Black)' rows (guide: no '(Black)'), 'Flat White (8oz)' ('Flat White Regular'), the five '... Oat Drink' coffees (guide: '... Oat Milk Drink'), and the two 'Sponge Sugar Paste 8"' rows (guide: '8"Round*' with an asterisk) = 31; plus 'Hazelnut Hot Chocolate with Cream' whose row marks milk only although its name says hazelnut (policy 3). JUDGEMENT CALLS for the founder: (1) 'Bacon (1 slice)', 'Black Pudding (1 slice)', 'Pork Link Sausage (1 sausage)' and 'Sliced Sausage (1 slice)' take the guide's rows 'Bacon', 'Black Pudding', 'Pork Link Sausage', 'Sliced Sausage' (same section, same name; only the printed portion differs; deleting the PORTION rule in baynes.py holds those four back instead). (2) 'Tea with Oat Drink' is recorded as may contain milk from the guide's general sentence about oat drinks although its own row has no star. (3) 'Gingerbread Latte with Cream & Sprinkles' stays published as printed (milk only, no gluten): in a drink 'gingerbread' is a flavour name, the accuracy audit does not flag it, but it is the one name that might be read the other way; add it to ALLERGEN_HOLDBACK in baynes.py if you prefer to hold it back. (4) The guide's own caveat applies to every row: it is derived from suppliers' specifications and the bakery cannot guarantee separation.
